tagline.text: The Subanen people's Danaw, a calm freshwater lake at the foot of the mountains

location.label: Location
location.text: Lakewood, Zamboanga del Sur (Poblacion and Biswangan)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,500–4,000 (day trip or one night from Pagadian, per person)

children.text: Lake Wood is a large freshwater lake in the municipality of Lakewood, Zamboanga del Sur. You can stroll along its shore, paddle a kayak or ride a bangka, and take in Subanen stories and lake-fish dishes along the way.

Lake Wood lies on the Zamboanga Peninsula of Mindanao, in Zamboanga del Sur between the municipalities of Lakewood and Kumalarang. According to Wikipedia, its surface area is about 7.4 square kilometers, its maximum depth about 85 m, and its surface elevation about 320 m above sea level. Blogs and local sources give 700–800 hectares, so figures differ by source; think of it simply as a lake big enough to give its name to a town. The lake is fed by rain and groundwater, and its only outlet, the Biswangan River, flows southeast into Dumanquilas Bay.

The indigenous Subanen people call the lake Danaw and regard it as part of their ancestral domain. The present name dates to 1904, when Captain Cornelius C. Smith of the U.S. Army's 14th Cavalry Regiment reported the lake to the American administration during an expedition from Misamis to Dumanquilas Bay; it was named after the then governor-general, Leonard Wood, and later shortened. Locals tell of a giant fish-like creature called the Busiso that lives in the lake, and there is a taboo against singing while sailing on the water.

The character of this destination is nothing like Boracay or El Nido. Instead of sandy beaches and polished facilities, the draw is quiet time: gazing at a lake ringed by rice fields and mountains and paddling out onto the water. Beside the lake in the Poblacion (town center) there is a paved walkway, and on the hillside in the Biswangan area there is a resort with good lake views.
Getting here means flying to Pagadian first and then continuing by road, so access is not easy. The lake is only about
42km

from Pagadian, though, so a day trip is possible, and if you stay overnight you can see the lake at both morning and sunset. Compared with famous lakes such as Lake Sebu, very few foreign visitors come, which gives the place a feel closer to everyday local life.

In the Poblacion section of Lakewood, a paved walkway runs along the lake. It is a pleasant place for an easy stroll at dusk to enjoy the mountains and the color of the water, and no entrance fee is known.
At Alindahaw Lakeview Resort you can rent a kayak and paddle yourself. A 2015 source listed kayaks at

Alindahaw Lakeview Resort in Biswangan is described as the best-known spot for viewing Lake Wood. It has rooms, infinity pools and a restaurant facing the lake, and works for both day visits and overnight stays. Room counts and facilities differ between sources, so check before you book.

blocks.title: The legend of Danaw and Subanen culture

children.text: The center of this place's story is that the Subanen call the lake Danaw and regard it as their ancestral land. Ask local residents politely about the Busiso legend and the singing taboo. Always ask permission before photographing rituals or village events.

Porang (the Mindanao rasbora, Rasbora philippina) is the only known endemic fish of the lake, and locally it is eaten along with carp as lake fish. Ask restaurants whether it is on the menu, and check the price first where freshly caught fish is sold.

On the hills around the lake, terraced rice paddies blend with tropical orchards. Depending on the season, fruits such as rambutan and lanzones appear, and you can taste seasonal fruit at the village market.

Within the municipality there are Baka Falls, another waterfall in Barangay Gasa, and a trekking route up Mount Sirungan, the municipality's highest peak. You can combine them with the lake on a two-day trip, but the roads are rough, so it is safer to use a local guide and a motorcycle taxi.
Take a van to Lakewood from the van terminal in downtown Pagadian. Vans leave roughly hourly, and departures can be delayed while cargo is loaded, so allow some slack.
You arrive at Lakewood town or the highway junction. The trip is usually described as taking around
1 hour 30 minutes
. If you got off at the junction, continue to town and the resort by habal-habal or van.
Walk the lakeside promenade in town and take in the view of the lake. Mornings are less sunny and the water tends to be calm.
Head to the resort in Biswangan and rent a kayak to get out on the lake. Check kayak and bangka rates by phone or with the resort beforehand.
Have lunch with lake fish or Filipino home cooking. The menu may vary from day to day.
Check the last van time and head back to Pagadian. If it rains the road becomes slippery, so it is best to leave early.
If a bus only goes as far as the junction, you are described as needing to continue a few kilometers more to reach town, so leave plenty of time for the return trip as well.

items.title: One-night lake getaway
items.subtitle: Sunset and a nearby trek the next day

children.text: Leave Pagadian by van and arrive in Lakewood before noon. After check-in, have lunch at a restaurant with a lake view.
Go kayaking or relax at the resort pool. Go out to a viewpoint or the promenade as the sun sinks over the lake.
Eat at the resort restaurant or a restaurant in town. The town reportedly has no major bank branches, so bring plenty of cash.
If you want to visit Baka Falls or trek Mount Sirungan, ask the municipal tourism contact to find a guide. If time is tight, you can just take a morning lake walk and return to Pagadian.
Cebu Pacific is known to operate nonstop flights from Manila (NAIA) to Pagadian Airport (PAG), taking about
1 hour 50 minutes
. Weekly frequencies and fares vary a lot by season, so check on a booking site.
Pagadian Airport is about
5km
from the city center. Operations were suspended in April 2024 for runway repairs, so check whether service has resumed and read the latest notices.
From Cebu, Cebgo flies to Pagadian.
If flights do not fit your plans, you can also travel overland via Cebu or Cagayan de Oro, but it takes a long time.
Vans to Lakewood run from the van terminal in downtown Pagadian roughly hourly and are described as taking about
1 hour 30 minutes
. I could not confirm the fare, so ask locally.
The distance from Pagadian to Lakewood is about
42km
. Vans and jeepneys run to the transport terminal in town.

Large buses sometimes go only as far as the Lakewood junction on the national highway (the Kumalarang-side junction); from there you must continue to town and the resort by van or habal-habal (modified motorcycle).
Tricycles run on the paved circumferential road in town.
On unpaved mountain roads and to the falls and mountain, habal-habal is often the only option; drivers can be hard to find, so ask your lodging or the town hall to connect you.
You can also cross the lake by bangka.
Lakewood's elevation is not low, so daytime highs are around
and nighttime lows around
, which feels cool, and annual rainfall is reported at about 1,094 mm. Rain is frequent, so an umbrella or raincoat is practically essential.
For lake views, photography and kayaking, the drier
December–May
is the most comfortable. In the rainy season roads turn muddy and visibility over the lake can be hazy.

Alindahaw Lakeview Resort, on the hillside in Biswangan, is the most widely described place to stay. It offers lake-view rooms, pools and kayak rentals, and is good for watching sunrise and sunset over the lake. Operating status, rates and room counts differ between sources, so confirm by phone or social media before you visit. The town has few large hotels, so in the busy season you can also stay in a Pagadian hotel and visit on a day trip.

Meals center on the resort restaurant and small eateries in town. Worth trying are freshwater fish dishes such as lake carp and porang, and Filipino home cooking using garden vegetables. At the market you can buy seasonal fruit such as rambutan and lanzones. The town reportedly has no major bank branches, so get your cash in Pagadian beforehand.
Check before leaving what time vans from Pagadian stop running. For a day trip, a schedule that gets you back early in the afternoon is safer.
Bring plenty of cash. The town is reported to have no major bank branches.
Bring an umbrella and a waterproof bag. Rain is frequent all year, and one visitor account describes getting soaked on the way back.
Wear a life jacket on the lake, and avoid loud singing out of respect for the local taboo.
Ask permission first before photographing Subanen homes, rituals or events.
Habal-habal drivers can be hard to find, so ask your lodging or the town hall tourism contact to connect you.
The Alindahaw Festival is described as held every year, but I could not confirm its date. To time your visit, ask the Lakewood town hall.
Mobile signal and electricity can be unreliable in outlying villages, so bring a power bank.
Before traveling, check your government's travel advisories and security notices for Mindanao. Fares and transport details in this guide mix in older sources and need to be confirmed locally.
The road from the highway into town and the mountain roads are slippery in the rainy season, and some sections are unpaved. Finish your travel before dark.
Weather can change suddenly for swimming or kayaking, so get out of the water immediately if the wind rises or thunder sounds.
Emergency care is reportedly referred to hospitals in Pagadian, so bring your own basic medicines.
Pagadian Airport suspended operations in 2024 for runway repairs, so check the latest operating notices.
Resorts and restaurants may change their operating status, so contact them directly to confirm before you visit.
A waterfall within the municipality of Lakewood. It is fairly close to the lake, but the road can be rough, so use a habal-habal and a guide, and
confirm the exact location and access with the town hall
The highest mountain in Lakewood, at whose foot the lake lies. A trekking route is reported, and it is safer to go with a guide.
The provincial capital and gateway city, with the airport, port and hotels. Lakewood is about
1 hour 30 minutes
away by van.
Trekking and cycling routes are described as running from Biswangan to Gasa. Check route conditions and distances locally.
